note: From the 2026-08-05 register-first pass on the MASAF national register (53 entries for comune Napoli) plus Campania's regional register. Leads failed only our evidence bar, the count, or the walkable-cluster test; blocked can never ship as they stand. The register's 53 entries are not a count of Naples' monumental trees, only of what is registered.

leads.name: The False Kapok of the Orto Botanico
leads.why: The largest registered tree in Naples at 880 cm girth (800 cm in Campania's regional register, scheda 165) and 25 m tall, over 100 years old, with the spined bottle trunk the species is famous for. Two sources already agree on it. It is a lead only because it belongs to a different cluster: the Orto Botanico is 1.2 km downhill from the Real Bosco, entry is free but by booking during limited weekday hours, and putting one booking-only garden into a free-park walk breaks the walk. The Orto Botanico deserves its own cluster page, see the group entry below.

leads.name: The Orto Botanico cluster (six further registered trees)
leads.species: Nolina longifolia 560 cm, Quercus crenata 440 cm, Eucalyptus globulus 440 cm, Ginkgo biloba 300 cm, Jubaea chilensis 250 cm, Brahea roezlii 190 cm
leads.why: Seven individually registered trees inside 150 metres, which would be the tightest cluster on the site, in the botanical garden Michele Tenore founded in 1807. The Quercus crenata is a natural cork-and-turkey-oak hybrid and genuinely uncommon; the Jubaea chilensis is the Chilean wine palm, endangered at home. Not published now because access is free but booking-based with restricted hours, and because the garden's own website does not describe individual specimens, so the second source has to be found tree by tree. This is the obvious next Naples pass.

leads.name: The Cedar of Lebanon of the Principessa Jolanda Gardens
leads.why: 418 cm and 18 m, agreed exactly by the national register and Campania's regional register (scheda 23), whose coordinates fall 20 m apart. The gardens were built by Antonio Niccolini between 1832 and 1836, so the tree is probably about 190 years old, but no source dates the tree itself. Held back for one specific reason: a monumental plane on the same staircase was destroyed by lightning in August 2022 (see blocked), and no source published since then confirms this cedar still stands. Verify liveness and it belongs on the page, 350 m west of the Porta Grande.

leads.name: The Camphor of the Principessa Jolanda Gardens
leads.why: 388 cm in the national register. Corroborated only loosely, by a gardening site noting that a camphor and a cedar in these gardens are still monumental, with no date on the claim. Same liveness doubt as the cedar above after the 2022 lightning strike on the staircase plane. Also a fourth camphor would make the page repetitive.

leads.name: The Plane of the Pheasantry
leads.why: Inside the Real Bosco, on the route between the Garden of the Princes and the Real Fruttiera, so it would sit on the walk. Campania's regional register (scheda 250) dates it at 200 years and places it isolated in a circular plot west of the pheasantry, reached from the Porta Miano. Blocked from publication by an unresolved conflict: the regional register gives 170 cm girth and 25 m height, the national register gives 430 cm and 35 m for the same coordinate. A 2.5x disagreement on girth is too large to publish either way, and one measurement is probably a diameter or a different tree.

leads.name: The Magnolia of the Reggia di Capodimonte
leads.why: 540 cm girth and 19 m, the fourth largest registered tree in Naples and inside the free park on the northern walk. Single-sourced: the national register only, and the museum's own page on its monumental trees does not include it. It would also be the one tree here with a real seasonal peak, the large cream flowers in late spring, so it is worth a second source hunt.

leads.name: The Camphor of the Sant'Andrea delle Dame Cloister
leads.why: 500 cm and 25 m in the cloister of a sixteenth century convent now part of the university medical faculty, in the historic centre 1.5 km south of Capodimonte. Sacred ground, exactly the kind of site worth searching. Held back on two counts: single-sourced, and cloister access inside a working university building is unconfirmed, which hard rule 10 says means leave it out until someone establishes that a visitor may walk in.

leads.name: The Camphor of the Accademia di Belle Arti Cloister
leads.why: 300 cm and 28 m, tall for its girth, in the cloister of the fine arts academy. Same two problems as Sant'Andrea delle Dame: single-sourced and unconfirmed public access to an institutional courtyard.

leads.name: The Podocarpus of Piazza Cavour
leads.why: 242 cm and 25 m on a fully public square in the centre, so access is not the issue. Single-sourced in the national register, and it would sit alone 1.5 km from the Capodimonte cluster with nothing to walk to. A candidate for a future historic-centre cluster with the two cloister camphors, if their access resolves.

leads.name: The Eucalyptus of Piazza Vittoria
leads.why: 676 cm, 25 m, the third largest registered tree in Naples, on the Villa Comunale seafront with three registered oriental planes (439, 428 and 412 cm) within 250 m of it. That is a genuine second walkable cluster on the waterfront, 4 km south of Capodimonte, and probably the best next Naples pass after the Orto Botanico. All four are currently single-sourced.

leads.name: The Phytolacca of Via Manzoni
leads.why: 627 cm and only 10 m tall, the ombu, a South American giant herb rather than a true tree, which builds an enormous swollen soft-wooded base. Visually one of the strangest things in the register. Single-sourced, and out at Posillipo with nothing else near it.

blocked.name: The Plane of the Principessa Jolanda Staircase
blocked.reason: Dead. A century-old plane on the Scale della Principessa Jolanda was split in half by lightning and collapsed into the road during the storms of 23 to 24 August 2022, reported by the III Municipality councillor Carlo Restaino with photographs. The register still lists it at 396 cm. This is the monumental plane that stood at the centre of the staircase where the original design called for an obelisk.

blocked.name: The Citrus Grove of the Reggia di Capodimonte
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. The register files it as 'Insieme omogeneo di Citrus spp', a whole orchard rather than one tree, so there is no trunk to stand in front of. Note that the live city file publishes this as nap_006, 'The Historic Citrus Grove of the Bourbons', which fails the one-identifiable-tree test and should be retired.

blocked.name: The Canary Palms of the Mostra d'Oltremare
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as 'Insieme omogeneo', a group planting, not an individual tree.

blocked.name: The Ficus Group of the Accademia di Belle Arti Cloister
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as 'Insieme omogeneo di Ficus macrophylla', and additionally inside an institutional cloister with unconfirmed public access.

blocked.name: The Bird of Paradise Group at the Ospedale degli Incurabili
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point and not a tree. Registered as 'Insieme omogeneo di Strelitzia reginae', a bed of herbaceous plants, inside a hospital complex.

blocked.name: The Oriental Planes of the Orto Botanico, Via Foria
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as 'Insieme omogeneo di Platanus orientalis', an avenue planting along Via Foria.

blocked.name: The Washingtonia Group of the Sant'Andrea delle Dame Cloister
blocked.reason: Not a collectible point. Registered as 'Insieme omogeneo di Washingtonia robusta', a group planting, in a cloister with unconfirmed access.

blocked.name: The Cedar and Palm of the Palazzo Carbonelli di Letino
blocked.reason: Private ground. Both stand in the garden of a private palazzo on Corso Secondigliano with no evidence it is open to visitors, so hard rule 10 excludes them.

blocked.name: The Camphor of Miano, Via del Cimitero 1
blocked.reason: Access unconfirmed and address-level only. A 454 cm camphor at a numbered street address by a cemetery, with no source establishing whether it stands on public ground or in a private plot. Leave it out until that resolves.

blocked.name: The Pine of Posillipo (live nap_008)
blocked.reason: Already published and should not have been. The live city file dates it 'planted 1995', which makes it a 31-year-old tree on a site about ancient trees, and its pin is approximate. Not in any register. Flagged here so a merge does not carry it forward.
